As I'm going through with the editing on my current project that I hope to share with you all soon, I came across a pretty neat website called Hemingway Editor. You can find it here. You can either write directly through the interface or just copy and paste your work from your word processor of choice and it gets to work instantly.

It tells you how many words and sentences you have and, best of all, grades them on difficulty for you. It tells you if you've used too many adverbs, if you've used passive voice, and how many sentences are difficult (or extremely difficult) to read. There is a word of warning though; you want some sentences that are hard to read. If you end up removing all the adverbs and split up all the difficult sentences your work will read like a bad children's book. That's the major downside of the site. But it's a handy little tool if you have to take care of your own editing like I do.

Yes!
Hemingway is a fantastic tool for writers. I actually bought the application a while back and used it quite a bit on my first book. It was helpful in telling me how complicated my story was for readers and the likes. I'm a fan of adverbs personally, but I know they are supposed to be avoided. However, I'm a bit of a fluffer; I offer too much detail in certain scenarios for the sake of immersion.

+1 on the bad children's book comment.

Trial is moving forward in the Coral Ridge Mall shooting.

At a preliminary hearing on Tuesday, Judge Patrick Grady set arraignment for 22-year-old Alexander Kozak for July 2 at 2 p.m.

Kozak is accused of shooting 20-year-old Andrea Farrington of Cedar Rapids three times in the back while she was working a kiosk near the mall’s food court the night of June 12. He is being represented by public defender Peter Persaud.

Kozak had been employed by the mall’s security, Universal Protection Service, but they say he resigned earlier that morning. People close to Farrington have said Kozak had been bothering her for several weeks, including leaving notes on her car.

According to police, Kozak admitted post-Miranda to leaving the mall that day, going home to get a gun and returning with the intention of shooting Farrington.

Kozak is charged with 1st Degree Murder and faces a mandatory sentence of life in prison.
